subject.title: openai-responses transport sends null content, rejected by strict providers (400 schema error)

question: Should maintainers accept source inspection plus OpenAI SDK strict-mock proof for a narrow `content: null` Responses send-boundary sanitizer, or require another live strict-provider reproduction first?
rationale: The current source still lacks the sanitizer and the dependency contract excludes null content, but the direct fix PR closed because the contributor could not produce live weelinking proof and the exact reporter session shape has not been reproduced in CI.

options.title: Accept Targeted Sanitizer Proof
options.body: Sponsor or reopen a focused sanitizer fix using SDK strict-mock plus boundary regression tests, with live vendor proof treated as helpful but not required.

options.title: Require Live Strict-Provider Proof
options.body: Keep the issue blocked until the reporter or a maintainer with strict-provider credentials supplies redacted live logs showing before/after behavior.

options.title: Defer Normalization Policy
options.body: Leave the issue open as a maintainer design question until the team decides whether malformed message items should be repaired or dropped.

recommendation.title: Accept Targeted Sanitizer Proof
recommendation.body: Sponsor or reopen a focused sanitizer fix using SDK strict-mock plus boundary regression tests, with live vendor proof treated as helpful but not required.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenAI/Azure Responses transport work makes this the best available routing owner for the proof-scope and payload-policy choice.
